title: Steadyflow occupancy scout — intermittent throughput regression
content:
Context:
- Intermittent throughput drop observed on steadyflow pool (pool-id=sf-04) since 2025-01-12 deploy. Baseline 20K tokens/s -> drops to ~9–11K tokens/s for 10–30 minute windows, then recovers. No OOMs reported. CPU on host is stable. GPU utilization dips from 92% -> 35% during incidents.

High-level goal:
- Capture a reproducible trigger or at least reliable detection heuristics.
- Narrow to continuous-batching config or KV-cache interaction.

Quick observations from dashboards:
- Prefill_latency.p50 increases slightly (~5–10ms) before drop; prefill_latency.p95 spikes coincide with throughput dips.
- Active_requests count on router stays constant; queue depth on worker increases a bit (but not to throttling limits).
- KV-cache hit rate falls ~6% during incidents.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Continuous-batcher window drift + occupancy hysteresis: batch windows shift so many partially-filled windows are sent -> lower throughput under same concurrency.
2) KV cache eviction thrash when sequence length distribution changes -> more prefill work per request -> runtime enters smaller micro-batches.
3) Slow-to-wake worker (slab allocator state) causing temporary slot starvation -> reduces batching aggregation.
4) Autoscaling/capacity bleed (containers marked draining) -> routing to fewer workers with cold caches.

Commands / probes I ran (timestamps local):
- Collected live batch histograms on node t2-worker-08: curl -s http://t2-worker-08:9090/metrics | grep batch_window_size -> saw bimodal: 1 and 8 token windows during dip (2025-01-15T14:03).
- Dumped KV cache stats: curl -s http://t2-worker-08:9090/debug/kvstats -> hits 87%, misses 13% baseline; during dip 80/20.
- Triggered microtrace on runtime: /opt/ri/bin/trace-capture --duration 120s --filter=\"batch,kvcache,prefill\" -> collected trace file /tmp/trace-sf-14-01-15.pb.
- Replayed request set locally with envoy proxy to mimic latency distribution: python tools/replay_trace.py --trace /tmp/trace-sf-14-01-15.pb --concurrency 32 -> saw throughput collapse locally when prefill latencies hit p95>120ms.

Snippets from logs (redacted):
- 2025-01-15T14:02:33Z [serving-runtime] WARN batcher: window_expansion: occupancy=0.27 window_ms=5 -> flush_count=9
- 2025-01-15T14:02:37Z [kv-cache] INFO eviction: evicting 256 entries score=0.12
- 2025-01-15T14:02:40Z [serving-runtime] WARN slot_manager: slot-starvation-detected tid=0x7f3b  free_slots=2 inflight=30

What looks odd:
- batcher log: 'occupancy=0.27' repeatedly for ~3 minutes, while overall inflight requests unchanged. Suggests many small windows being flushed early.
- eviction bursts align with occupancy dips. Could be correlated (eviction causes more prefill work -> windows shrink) but direction unknown.

Quick experiments to run (next):
- Add a short-lived feature flag to slow down eviction bursts: kv_cache.eviction_aggressiveness -> 0.8 for a minute on pool sf-04. Watch throughput/kv-hit. (Risk: memory growth).
- Force batcher to use fixed-window mode for 5 min: batcher.mode=fixed_window_ms=8 -> see if occupancy stabilizes.
- Deploy a debug build with additional sampler logging for batch_window_selection (10% sampling) to collect richer traces without full perf impact.

Repro recipe (best-effort, low-risk):
1) On staging pool mimic traffic: use replay_trace.py with original inter-arrival times but punch a synthetic spike in sequence lengths (25% of requests with long sequences).
2) Observe KV cache hit rate and batch window distribution.
3) Toggle eviction aggressiveness and fixed-window mode.

Notes / sticky points:
- The problem tends to appear on pools running with compact-kv quantization profile. Haven't reproduced on FP16 pools yet. Suspect memory layout/eviction thresholds differ by profile.
- Autoscaler logs show scale events ~1m before several incidents, but not always. Need to cross-check router decisions (maybe transient draining).
- There is an open PR (#3281) that touched batcher heuristics; landed exactly at deploy time. Might be a red herring but deserves review.

Immediate actionable checklist (owner: Riley / ping Samir):
- [ ] Add ephemeral flag for kv eviction throttle on sf-04 (Samir to sign off DB mem risk).
- [ ] Roll batcher to fixed-window for canary subset (Riley).
- [ ] Correlate scheduler/container drain events with incidents (Maya).
- [ ] Attach collected trace /tmp/trace-sf-14-01-15.pb to JIRA INF-2048.
- [ ] If fixed-window removes regression, revert fix in PR #3281 and add unit test for occupancy hysteresis.

Questions for triage meeting:
- Is there a way to surface a per-pool "occupancy score" alert (p95 of occupancy < 0.4 for 5m) without creating noise?
- Should we prefer KV cache hysteresis (temporary holdback on eviction) over batcher conservative behaviour? Which is lower-risk for customer workloads?

Misc scratch ideas (brain dump):
- Add a lightweight servo that increases window_ms when kv-hit-rate drops below threshold, to allow more aggregation.
- Maintain a short-term ring buffer of recent window sizes and use exponential smoothing to avoid flip-flopping.
- Consider a tiny randomized jitter to eviction timestamps to avoid synchronized eviction storms across replicas.

Attachments / artifacts to include in ticket:
- /tmp/trace-sf-14-01-15.pb (trace capture)
- small replay trace: /tmp/replay-short-sf.pb
- grafana snapshot id: gfsnap-20250115-1405

Unresolved threads / follow-ups:
- Confirm if quantized pools use a different cache eviction policy (MAYA to confirm with infra team).
- Ask release-eng whether PR #3281 was rolled back in any clusters during emergency mitigation window.

Notes to self: log more context in future captures: include env vars (BATCHER_MAX_WINDOW_MS, KV_MAX_ENTRIES), heap usage snapshot and kernel slab stats.

End of scratchpad.
